papers.title: Axiomatic degree theory on topological manifolds
papers.abstract: In this note we study extension of standard Euclidean degree in nonlinear analysis to the setting of general oriented topological manifolds. The axiomatization of Euclidean degree is adapted to this setting. Existence and uniqueness are proven. The existence does not rely on smooth approximations as in the Euclidean case -- this is irrelevant for manifolds which do not admit a smooth structure and could be ambiguous for manifolds admitting many smooth structures. Rather, we rely on a cohomological approach using only topological information. When compared to the Euclidean case, we think this approach makes the proofs simpler and more transparent. The standard notion of a degree of maps between closed oriented manifolds studied in algebraic topology is recovered as a special case. A generalization of the notion of winding number is developed and related to the notion of degree. The familiar composition formula of the Euclidean degree is also obtained in this context.

papers.title: A zero-free strip for the $L$-functions of the elliptic curves $y^2=x^3+d$
papers.abstract:
For a nonzero integer $d$ let $E_d$ be the elliptic curve $y^2=x^3+d$ over $\mathbb Q$. Part I adapts OpenAI's $11/12$ argument to prove that $L(E_d,s)
e0$ for $\Re s>17/12$. Part II adapts OpenAI's $7/8$ argument to prove $L(s,\overline\alpha\eta)
e0$ for $\Re s>7/8$, where $\eta$ is any finite-order Hecke character of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and $\alpha(n)=n/|n|$ on primary generators. Consequently $L(E_d,s)
e0$ for $\Re s>11/8$. The analytic normalization is $L(E_d,s+ rac12)$, so the two boundaries are $11/12$ and $7/8$ within $0<\Re s<1$. The curve characters have infinite order, and require new transformation and moment arguments. These are proved here; steps identical to the original arguments are cited. Part II also uses the ideas from OpenAI's finite-order $7/8$ theorem. Higher-weight and symmetric-power extensions are discussed; more general CM forms are the subject of a second paper.

papers.title: An analogue of the Erdos-Kac theorem for signed Iwasawa invariants of modular forms
papers.abstract: Erdos and Kac proved that the number of distinct prime factors of an integer has a Gaussian limiting distribution. We prove an analogue for the signed Iwasawa invariants of non-ordinary weight-two modular forms. Under the hypotheses of this paper, we construct infinitely many forms congruent to a given form $g$ that realize every common nonnegative increase of its two signed $\lambda$-invariants. We count the levels realizing each increase. In the resulting family, the common increase is asymptotically Gaussian, with mean and variance $\delta_\Pi\log\log X+O_g(1)$ for a positive constant $\delta_\Pi$.

papers.title: An order-five Haagerup--Izumi vertex operator algebra at central charge eight
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit unitary strongly rational vertex operator algebra $U$ of central charge eight inside $V_{A_4\oplus A_4}$ and identify $Rep(U)$ with the Drinfeld center of the positive order-five Haagerup--Izumi category. The construction adjoins one algebraic weight-two field to a diagonal affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ at level forty and the ambient conformal vector. Exact finite lattice identities imply strong generation and $C_2$-cofiniteness. A finite integral order in the actual Zhu algebra descends semisimplicity from a $1590$-dimensional upper presentation over $\mathbb F_{10069}$. To determine the modules, we combine the good-prime block bound with lattice character growth and a Wronskian inequality. The resulting full branching has an irreducible congruence complement of dimension at most fifteen; its exact classification forces all fourteen denominator-$29$ sectors. Finally, the actual holomorphic $E_8$ extension determines the boundary fusion category and its associator. The proof is computer-assisted, with exact arithmetic certificates separated from exploratory numerical evidence.

papers.title: Gonality and quintic points on intermediate modular curves
papers.abstract: For $\{\pm 1\}\subseteq\Delta\subseteq(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^\times$ let $X_\Delta(N)$ be the intermediate modular curve between $X_1(N)$ and $X_0(N)$. We determine the $\mathbb{Q}$-gonality of every strict intermediate curve $X_\Delta(N)$ with $N\le 50$, and of $X_1(N)$ for $41\le N\le 50$, where it equals the upper bound of Derickx and van Hoeij at every level. We also settle the thirty levels left open by Derickx, Hwang, Jeon and Orli\'c, completing the list of curves $X_0(N)$ with infinitely many points of degree $5$, and we show that exactly $43$ strict intermediate curves have infinitely many points of degree $5$. As a consequence, the strict intermediate curves of density degree $5$ are exactly the four $\mathbb{Q}$-pentagonal curves found by Orli\'c. The proofs use published classifications, the Castelnuovo--Severi inequality, and three computational methods; all computations can be rerun from the accompanying code.

papers.title: Hilbert functions of chopped ideals of general plane points
papers.abstract: Let I be an ideal generated by general forms of degree d in a polynomial ring. We study its Hilbert function, multiplication by powers of a general linear form, and its generic initial ideal. The principal estimate concerns products of homogeneous subspaces: if A ⊆ Se, B ⊆ Sd, ASd−e ⊆ B, and codim B ≤ codim A, then dim(AB)/ dim Sd+e ≥ dim A/ dim Se whenever d ≥ 2e. The resulting bounds for catalecticant rank loci, together with corresponding bounds in S/(zk ), give Fröberg’s predicted Hilbert function and maximal rank for every power of a general linear form through degree d + e, over any infinite field. In characteristic zero, the Expected Syzygy Conjecture for general points also gives an almost reverse lexicographic generic initial ideal in this range. Under the same conjecture, a deformation of ideals generated by forms vanishing at general points gives the predicted Hilbert function and maximal rank for multiplication by a linear form through degree 2d, together with all power maps whose source degree is at most d.

papers.title: Non-Archimedean Hudzik-Landes-Dragomir-Kato-Saito-Tamura Inequality
papers.abstract: In 1992, Hudzik and Landes \textit{[Math. Ann.]} derived a breakthrough generalization of the triangle inequality for two nonzero elements in normed linear spaces, which was generalized to finitely many nonzero elements independently in 2006 by Dragomir \textit{[Bull. Aust. Math. Soc.]} and in 2007 by Kato, Saito and Tamura \textit{[Math. Inequal. Appl]}. We derive a non-Archimedean version of Hudzik-Landes-Dragomir-Kato-Saito-Tamura inequality.

papers.title: Point Density Measures: A Measure-Theoretic Framework with Applications to Geometric Probability
papers.abstract: The notion of point density is widely used in geometry, probability, sampling theory, computational science, and spatial statistics to describe the distribution of discrete point sets. Although commonly interpreted as the number of points per unit volume, the concept is often used without a unified measure-theoretic formulation, leading to ambiguities between counting measures, empirical measures, sampling measures, intensity measures, and density functions. This paper develops a unified measure-theoretic framework centered on the concept of a \emph{point density measure}, regarded as the intrinsic mathematical object describing the spatial distribution of point density over a measurable space. Counting measures and empirical measures are considered as fundamental constructions associated with discrete point sets, while point density functions arise only when the corresponding point density measure is absolutely continuous with respect to a prescribed reference measure, in which case they are obtained through the Radon--Nikodym theorem. The framework clarifies the relationships among these measure-theoretic objects and provides a consistent mathematical language for deterministic point configurations and probabilistic sampling procedures. As an application, Bertrand's paradox is reinterpreted within this framework by viewing the classical sampling procedures as inducing different point density measures on a common measurable parameter space. The resulting probability measures are obtained by normalization of the corresponding point density measures, illustrating that the differing probabilities arise from different choices of underlying measures rather than from an inconsistency in probability theory. The proposed framework provides a unified perspective on point distributions with potential applications in geometric probability, stochastic geometry, spatial statistics, computational geometry, sampling theory, image analysis, and point cloud processing.

papers.title: Strongly regular graphs on 160, 232, 261 and 280 vertices from fusions of orbitals of PΓL(2,8) and 2^4:(S3×S3)
papers.abstract: We construct strongly regular graphs with parameters (160,54,18,18), (232,63,14,18), (261,64,14,16) and (280,63,14,14), and hence also their complements. All four parameter sets were marked "?" (existence unknown) in Brouwer's online table on 11 and 12 October 2026; they are the parameters of the hypothetical partial geometries pg(9,5,3), pg(7,8,2), pg(8,7,2) and pg(9,6,2). We give eight pairwise non-isomorphic graphs: three on 160 vertices, one on 232, two on 261 and two on 280. None of them is geometric. As far as we can determine, they are the first graphs known with these parameters. Five of the graphs have a short description over the projective line PG(1,8) and its quadratic extension PG(1,64). The vertices are pairs of points of PG(1,8) or conjugate pairs of points of PG(1,64) ∖ PG(1,8), each carrying a label in 𝔽_8*, together with a small orbit of points, pairs, or conjugate pairs. Adjacency is decided by cross ratios: for two labelled vertices on disjoint pairs, the quotient (or the product) of the two labels must equal the cross ratio of the two pairs or its inverse; for pairs sharing a point it must equal 1, and a labelled pair and a conjugate pair are adjacent when their cross ratio is a primitive cube root of unity. The "quotient" graphs on 232, 261 and 280 vertices have the automorphism group (SL(2,8) × C_7) ⋊ C_6 ≅ GL(2,8) ⋊ C_6 of order 21168; the two "product" graphs have C_2 × PΓL(2,8), of order 3024. One graph on 160 vertices lives on the 16 cells of a 4 × 4 grid and three copies of the 48 flags of its even transversals; its automorphism group is C_3 × 2^4:(S_3 × S_3), of order 1728. The other two graphs on 160 vertices have automorphism groups of orders 1728 and 576. The graphs were found by a computer search over fusions of orbitals of groups acting with two or three orbits, using the GAP library of tables of marks; the search reported five graphs, and enumerating all fusions of the same group actions gave three more. We do not classify the graphs with these parameters. The same constructions over PG(1,q) give, for q=4, the classical skew-lines graph of PG(3,2) and a second known srg(35,16,6,8), and no strongly regular graph for q=16 or q=32 under the groups searched (complete solver verdicts): within this model the graphs for q=8 appear to be sporadic. Strong regularity of every graph is checked by an exact, standalone, standard-library Python program, the constructions are re-implemented from the text of this paper, and all computer results were reproduced by an independent audit with separately written code and checked again by a referee with its own code. Also deposited on Zenodo with the full data archive (the citable record): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23313399

papers.title: The Chaise Longue Theorem: Conjecture 1.2 of Degtyarev–Shimada for the Fermat varieties of every degree in every even dimension, and the integral Hodge conjecture for those whose degree is prime, equal to 4, or prime to (n+1)!
papers.abstract: Let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^{n+1}$ be the complex Fermat variety of degree $m \ge 3$ and even dimension $n = 2k$, and let $L(X) \subseteq H_n(X; \mathbb{Z})$ be the subgroup generated by the classes of its standard $k$-dimensional linear subspaces. Degtyarev and Shimada conjectured that $H_n(X; \mathbb{Z})/L(X)$ is torsion free [DS, Conjecture 1.2]. We prove this conjecture for every degree $m \ge 3$ in every even dimension, modulo two topological results used by [DS]: Pham's theorem on the homology of the affine Fermat variety, and their intersection numbers. Its algebraic form — the quotient $\mathbb{Z}[G]/(\psi_J)$ of the group ring of [DS] is free abelian of rank $m^{2k+1} - Q_k(m)$ — is proved with no topology, and it has been verified for every degree by a complete proof in the proof assistant Lean 4 with the Mathlib library, with no gap and no axiom beyond the three standard ones. The proof reduces the conjecture, prime by prime, to dimension counts in truncated polynomial rings, proved by peeling off one variable at a time. Consequences: the integral Hodge conjecture for $X$ whenever $m$ is prime, or $m = 4$, or $m$ is prime to $(n+1)!$, with the integral Hodge classes of middle degree generated by the standard linear subspaces — in particular for the Fermat quartic of every even dimension; and the primitivity of the sublattices spanned by the linear subspaces that [DS] exhibit on the partial Fermat varieties, which [DS] proved conditionally on the conjecture. This work has not been refereed by a human expert.

papers.title: The truncated octahedral conjecture
papers.abstract: Among three-dimensional parallelohedra of fixed volume, the Archimedean truncated octahedron uniquely minimizes surface area, affirming a conjecture of K. Bezdek from 2006. One inequality in the proof is verified by an exact computer-assisted certificate. The simplex, frame, and graphical-zonotope inequalities used in the proof hold in arbitrary dimension.
